The Historian

By: Kate Barry | Commission

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Is it an Egyptian? Is it a Roman? Is it Napoleon? Get ready to suspend your disbelief and step back in time with a man on a mission.

Unique Selling Point:
Gareth Sephton (24) is a unique character with a passion for history who believes he is fulfilling “my dutiful mission to bring the wisdom of the past back to the present.”
He has decided to literally put himself in the shoes of people who lived before us, to experience what life was like for them.

On any random afternoon one may spot him in the Botanical Gardens: an Inca warrior, an Ottoman trader, a German WWI officer, a knighted Crusader patrolling the forests. Some dog walkers look confused and hurry by; others stop to find out what it's all about and learn some facts; some dogs take exception and go in for the kill. Gareth believes history is more than just memorising a string of facts - for him learning is a sensory experience: one must immerse yourself in the textures, and tastes of a period to truly understand what it was like for our predecessors.


Summary:
Gareth took History as a subject in high school, but has not studied the subject at tertiary level as he believes the syllabus is skewed. Instead he immerses himself in books, podcasts, videos, and online articles, and speaking to people about their experiences. He calls it "engaging with history".
He threw out his television, and turned his TV room into his History Room. This is where he does his research and sews all the outfits that he wears. He now has almost 80 outfits, including shoes, head dress, weapons and other historical items.

On weekends he likes to spend an entire day in the park, immersing himself in a particular period. He sets up camp, eats period food, etc.

Further information:
Gareth pursues his passion full time, and manages to make a living out of being The Historian. He runs the History Club at Blairgowrie Primary School, where children spend and hour immersed in play and learning. His aim is to spark an interest in history for children.
He also visits 3 retirement homes a week, where the elderly enjoy his shows and chats.

Gareth is a unique character, who almost seems to have mistakenly landed in 21st Century Joburg from another time and place.

Script:


THE HISTORIAN

V/O: Saturday afternoon in Johannesburg Botanical Gardens: it’s laid-back and quiet – too quiet.

Sfx: Dogs barking

V/O: Who goes there? Or WTF - in the Roman alphabet.
Is that a member of the Praetorian Guard? From… across the Jukskei?

Roman: My name is Gaius Septimus. I signed up during the time of Caesar Traianius, yes? Emperor Trajan. The Emperor was a good man. He expanded the borders of the Empire.

Opening Link: When we first saw a man wandering around Emmarentia Park dressed as a Roman legionary, we thought no man, this must be a joke. Or a costume party that had spilled over from the night before. But when we started asking questions, we discovered something much deeper – one of Johannesburg’s truly unique characters. So come with me as we step into the past and meet The Historian.

V/O: We find him over 3000 years ago, in the Temple of Blairgowrie.

Gareth: I’m actually dressed in an outfit of an official from the 14th Century BC, so the 1300’s. My Egyptian name is, Ahmose.

Govan: What?

Gareth: Ahmose.

Govan: What's that?

Gareth: It is, a very, fairly common name in Egypt, but I was given it by my father. And you'll find that all my outfits have their own names and even equivalent. So, my German name is Gerhardt. My French name is Gerard, and my Arabic name is Latif. It doesn't sound like a G, but Latif means gentle, and so does my name Gareth.

V/O: Gareth Sephton is unlike any other 24-year-old you’re likely to meet. He spends more time wearing historical outfits, than the clothing of today. But under all these different characters, he has a very clear understanding of his own character.
00:04:51
Gareth: When I was a child I always had this thing about fixating on things. I would find something and fixate on it. Obsess over it. It was space when I was a toddler. Then it became dinosaurs. So that set in motion today. I find an era and I fixate on it, learn it inside and out and create the outfit.

V/O: Gareth is a man on a mission.

Gareth: So, I call it mission ism. It's this mission that I'm on, and I'm very, I'm very serious about. I've given my life to it.

Govan: You're serious about it?

Gareth: Absolutely. I mean, is this not serious enough for you?

Govan: So, so what exactly is it about?

Gareth: So, oh, I take this thing off. I'll. I'll tell you how it works soon. So, this mission I'm on is all dictated by theory that I had back in 2019.

And the theory goes that when the universe began, matter was set in motion. Matter in motion has trajectory, a direction that it's headed in. This, trajectory, this momentum of the past has forged today, and it's busy forging the future. So, when I realized this, I thought to myself that how important it is to know the past, to know where we are today. I don't believe in time travel. This is the closest you'll get, is wearing the things they wore, eating the things they ate. I do believe the past is gone. It's inaccessible. And that's why I make outfits from history as a way to try and understand the momentum of the past.

Govan: Bro, that’s too deep for the outfits that you wear.

V/O: To give momentum to mission ism, he started a YouTube channel where he posts videos of his adventures back in time. He spends hours filming and editing these himself, and his home-made outfits span all of history: from the Stone Age to the Bronze Age, the Iron Age to the Middle Ages, the Modern Ages and back to the Stoned Age.

Gareth: I’m on nearly 80 outfits. I will hit my 80th when I finish my latest one I’m making.

Gareth: This used to be a TV room, but I got rid of the TV years ago. I had no need for the TV. When you got this to entertain yourself – threw the TV out and now became the History Room.

Govan: Did you make this yourself?

Gareth: So, this is my Knights Templar outfit. Everything is homemade, except the mail.

Govan: But this is probably the most important part of the whole room, ja?

Gareth: This is the heart. This is my sewing machine that I’ve had for many years. I went on a sewing course two years ago. So yeah, they taught me how to sew. So, I make all of my garments from scratch, and a lot of them… take for example – this is my latest. This is a Viking tunic.

Govan: Oh wow!

Gareth: Just worn by your everyday man in Scandinavia in the 10th century.

Govan: Is that the correct material?

Gareth: And this is the correct material, wool.

Sfx: Knight marching

Gareth: This is my Third Crusade Knights Templar outfit from 1189.

Govan: Did you study History at University?

Gareth: Not university. I’ve heard a lot about university, and I just felt like even just the culture, I didn’t blend in. Let’s say in my free time I make sewing.

Govan: Yeah.

Gareth: Most of my generation, they’re out at the bar at night. I prefer to sit at home and sew, listening to Mozart.

V/O: The mission is Gareth’s full-time occupation. To earn an income, he runs the History Club at Blairgowrie Primary School.

Gerhard: It’s okay, I’m fine!

V/O: The History Club members range from Grade 1 to Grade 6. Today they’re in Medieval Saxony.

Gerhard: What caused the Black Death?
Listen closely, I might quiz you later. It was caused by the rats coming from the ships that were trading, which on the rats were fleas, which inside their fleas were bacteria. Which inside the bacteria was yersinia pestis.
Yersinia pestis. Jawohl!

Link: So, I did History in school, but I don’t remember it being anything like this. And that’s because what Gareth is doing isn’t merely teaching history with names and dates. He’s doing it with these outfits, with food, with music, and sometimes with a bit of a dodgy accent.

V/O: But the kids don’t seem to mind, and they all respond to him with uninhibited delight.

Fight: Gareth injured.


V/O: This isn’t the only time he’s been injured in battle. While riding his noble steed in Delta Park, he took a tumble.

Gareth: Ready!

Sfx: Gareth falls.

Gareth: For the Holy Land and the Pope!

V/O: This mishap with the bicycle battalion could explain why the 3rd Crusade never reached Jerusalem.

Music: 1812 Overture

V/O: Not long after the fall of Delta - and three stitches and a black eye later - Gareth is on his way to Fountains Care Assisted Living. It’s one of three retirement villages he visits every week.

Gareth: My name is Gerard, and I am a fusilier in Napoleon’s grande armée, his grand army, oui. When I say oui, you must say oui. Oui?

Crowd: Oui!

Link: Living in an old-aged home doesn’t come with much excitement but Gareth certainly brings the difference – and he’s teaching these residents something that most of us have already forgotten. That’s remembering how to play.

Nicole: He’s really enjoyable. And he brings a quality here that we can’t find, I don’t think anywhere else. Ja, he’s amazing.

Anthony: I mean you can play bingo and put numbers here and there - dong, dong – which we do. This is something really special.

V/O: Whether special or special needs, The Historian is a gem bursting with creativity. With his self-made outfits, his self-taught musicianship and unshakeable belief in his mission, Gareth has carved a niche that is sparking interest in young and old.
And the rest, as they say, is history.
